where: Section 3, memory map; Exam trap 1; Quiz Q6
problem: The chapter presents addresses 80-FF as 'the upper 128 bytes of RAM' of the 8051, but the lead and the figure say the 8051 has only 128 bytes of data RAM (00-7F). The upper 128 bytes at 80-FF exist only on the 8052/8032 family; on a plain 8051, 80-FF is SFR space only. As written, trap 1 ('to read RAM byte 0x80 use @R0') and Q6 describe an 8052 as if it were the 8051, so the chapter contradicts itself.
fix: Keep the 8051 map as RAM 00-7F (direct and indirect) and SFRs 80-FF (direct only). Add one line: 'Parts in the 8052 family add a second 128 bytes of RAM at 80-FF that is reachable only indirectly; on a plain 8051 nothing is there but SFRs.' Then label trap 1 and Q6 as 8052 behaviour.

where: Section 1 and Section 3 (code fetch and PSEN)
problem: Saying 'a code fetch drives PSEN' and 'Code: 0000-0FFF, fetched with PSEN' is misleading. PSEN is activated only when code is fetched from external program memory. With EA high, fetches from the internal 4 KB ROM do not drive PSEN at all, and the chapter itself explains EA low/high in the traps.
fix: Write: 'A fetch from external program memory drives PSEN; fetches from the internal ROM do not. Data reads and writes drive RD or WR.'

problem: 'Move SP (say to 30)' mixes radix. Everywhere else the chapter writes 0x30, and bare 30 reads as decimal 30 = 1EH, which is inside register bank 3 — the opposite of what the advice intends. A student following it literally corrupts a bank.
fix: Write 'move SP to 0x30 (30H), so the first push lands at 0x31'.

problem: 'Some syllabi call this list the pin diagram and the register list below the SFR map. Only a few universities teach it pin by pin.' is vague and reads like filler; 'the register list below the SFR map' does not match anything in the chapter.
fix: Drop it, or replace with one concrete line: 'Pin numbering matters for wiring: P0.0 is pin 39, P1.0 is pin 1, and the control pins sit at the top of the package.'
